summary: This clipped documentation page describes the H3_COVERAGE geospatial function, which returns an ARRAY of INTEGER H3 cell IDs forming the minimal set of cells that completely cover a GEOGRAPHY input shape. It covers the syntax, the arguments (a GEOGRAPHY expression and a target resolution from 0 to 15), the return value, a usage note that cells are included when their boundary intersects the shape, and one example that covers a polygon at resolution 8. Navigation and boilerplate on the page were ignored.
one_line: Reference for the H3_COVERAGE function, which returns the minimal set of H3 cell IDs covering a geography shape at a given resolution.
key_facts: H3_COVERAGE returns an ARRAY of INTEGER values identifying the minimal set of H3 cells that completely cover a specified GEOGRAPHY object.
The geography_expression argument must be a GEOGRAPHY object.
The target_resolution argument must be an INTEGER between 0 and 15 (inclusive), specifying the H3 resolution of the returned cells.
Specifying any INTEGER value outside the 0 to 15 range results in an error.
A cell is included in the result set if its boundary intersects the input shape.
The example passes a Polygon with corners at (-122.481889 37.826683), (-122.479487 37.808548), (-122.474150 37.808904) and (-122.476510 37.826935) to H3_COVERAGE at resolution 8.
The example polygon's H3_COVERAGE result at resolution 8 contains six cell IDs, starting with 613196571542028287.
The example query aliases the result column as set_of_h3_cells_covering_polygon.
The page is categorized under the Geospatial functions group, with related sections on Conversion, Constructor, Accessor, Relationship and Measurement, Transformation, Utility and H3.
